Meta-analysis physiological costs of hibernation: Report 1 - OS Hibernation

Pablo Capilla-Lasheras

2026-05-04

This R Markdown Notebook contains the initial meta-analysis for the project ‘physiological ’costs’ of hibernation. Specifically, the meta-analysis of hibernation

Dataset and calculation of effect sizes

The dataset for this meta-analysis has been collected from the literature and curated by Pablo Burraco, Marko Prokic and Tamara Petrovic. It contains data on physiological effects of hibernation in different systems. Here a quick snapshot of the first lines of the dataset:

# dataset with raw data
data <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(
  here(
    "./01_data/raw_data/Hibernation_dataset_4_3_hibernation.xlsx"
  ),
  colNames = T,
  sheet = 1
)

paged_table(data, options = list(rows.print = 20))

As a summary of the initial dataset:

  • Number of studies: 61
  • Number of species: 28

For this initial meta-analysis, I am going to include all oxidative stress (OS) markers and calculate the standarised mean difference (g; with heteroscedastic population variances) as the effect size of analysis comparing hibernation versus euthermia. Positive SMD values indicate higher OS values in hibernation while negative SMD indicate lower OS values in hibernation. This is a summary of the effect size calculation based on the dataset above:

# ES data
data <- readRDS(
  here(
    "./01_data/processed_RDS_data_files/01_OS_metaanalysis_hibernation_full_data.RDS"
  )
)
data$obsID <- 1:nrow(data) # observation ID

# handling species names for phylogenetic-controlled models
data$Species <- replace_values(
  data$Species,
  "Myotis_pilosus" ~ "Myotis_ricketti" # correcting synomyn names manuallty
)

data$scientific_name <- gsub(
  x = data$Species,
  pattern = "_",
  replacement = " "
)

data$scientific_name_phylo <- data$scientific_name

## data for SMD
df_SMD <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(SMDH)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(SMDH.sv))

# matrix with phylogentic correlations
phylo_cor <- readRDS(
  here(
    "./01_data/processed_RDS_data_files/01_OS_phylogenetic_correlations_hibernation.RDS"
  )
)

phylo_tree <- readRDS(
  here(
    "./01_data/processed_RDS_data_files/01_OS_phylogenetic_tree_hibernation.RDS"
  )
)

tree <- ggtree(phylo_tree, size = 1.2) +
  xlim_tree(c(0, 35)) +
  geom_tiplab(
    aes(
      label = paste0(
        "italic('",
        sub(x = label, pattern = "_", replacement = " "),
        "')"
      )
    ),
    parse = TRUE,
    offset = 0.5,
    size = 5,
    hjust = 0
  )

ggsave(
  filename = here(
    "./03_plots/01_hibernation/00a_OS_phylo_tree.png"
  ),
  plot = tree,
  device = "png",
  height = 150,
  width = 90,
  units = "mm"
)

ggsave(
  filename = here(
    "./03_plots/01_hibernation/00a_OS_phylo_tree.pdf"
  ),
  plot = tree,
  height = 150,
  width = 90,
  units = "mm"
)

Summary of SMD effect size and number of observations included in the meta-analysis:

summary(df_SMD$SMDH)
##      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max. 
## -13.79044  -0.91954   0.04767   0.03417   0.93321  12.91844
print(tree)

  • Number of observation with non-missing SMD: 742
  • Number of studies in the dataset for analysis: 54
  • Number of species in the dataset for analysis: 26

Initial meta-analysis:

This initial model contains only the intercept and four random effects to account for phylogenetic variation and variation between and within studies beyond sampling variance.

## calculate var-cover matrix to control for correlated effect sizes within study and tissue
V <- vcalc(
  vi = SMDH.sv,
  cluster = Study_ID,
  subgroup = Tissue,
  grp1 = Hib_M,
  grp2 = Euthermia_M,
  w1 = Hib_N,
  w2 = Euthermia_N,
  data = df_SMD
)

# model
model_SMD <- rma.mv(
  yi = SMDH,
  V = V,
  mods = ~1,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | scientific_name_phylo,
    ~ 1 | Species,
    ~ 1 | obsID,
    ~ 1 | Study_ID
  ),
  data = df_SMD,
  R = list(scientific_name_phylo = phylo_cor),
  method = "REML",
  control = list(optimizer = "BFGS"),
  verbose = F
)
saveRDS(
  object = model_SMD,
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/01a_metamodel_hibernation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
model_SMD <- readRDS(
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/01a_metamodel_hibernation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
summary(model_SMD)
## 
## Multivariate Meta-Analysis Model (k = 733; method: REML)
## 
##     logLik    Deviance         AIC         BIC        AICc   
## -1343.9095   2687.8191   2697.8191   2720.7980   2697.9017   
## 
## Variance Components:
## 
##             estim    sqrt  nlvls  fixed                 factor    R 
## sigma^2.1  0.0759  0.2756     26     no  scientific_name_phylo  yes 
## sigma^2.2  0.1755  0.4189     26     no                Species   no 
## sigma^2.3  1.1242  1.0603    733     no                  obsID   no 
## sigma^2.4  0.0000  0.0051     54     no               Study_ID   no 
## 
## Test for Heterogeneity:
## Q(df = 732) = 2705.1175, p-val < .0001
## 
## Model Results:
## 
## estimate      se     zval    pval    ci.lb   ci.ub    
##  -0.1328  0.1865  -0.7123  0.4763  -0.4984  0.2327    
## 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
i2_SMD <- round(i2_ml(model_SMD), digits = 4) # heterogeneity random effects

Proportion of variation left after accounting for sampling variance and proportion accounted by each random effect:

knitr::kable(
  x = data.frame(
    Variable = names(i2_SMD),
    i2_value_percentage = as.numeric(round(i2_SMD, digits = 3))
  )
) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = F)

Publication bias: small-study effects

df_SMD$inv_eff_ss <- (1 / df_SMD$Hib_N) + (1 / df_SMD$Euthermia_N)

model_SMD_pb <- rma.mv(
  yi = SMDH,
  V = V,
  mods = ~ 1 + sqrt(inv_eff_ss),
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | scientific_name_phylo,
    ~ 1 | Species,
    ~ 1 | obsID,
    ~ 1 | Study_ID
  ),
  data = df_SMD,
  R = list(scientific_name_phylo = phylo_cor),
  method = "REML",
  control = list(optimizer = "BFGS"),
  verbose = F
)
saveRDS(
  object = model_SMD_pb,
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/06a_pb_metamodel_hibernation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
model_SMD_pb <- readRDS(
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/06a_pb_metamodel_hibernation_OS.RDS'
  )
)

summary(model_SMD_pb)

Publication bias: time-lag effects

df_SMD$year_scl <- scale(df_SMD$Year)

model_SMD_tl <- rma.mv(
  yi = SMDH,
  V = V,
  mods = ~ 1 + year_scl,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | scientific_name_phylo,
    ~ 1 | Species,
    ~ 1 | obsID,
    ~ 1 | Study_ID
  ),
  data = df_SMD,
  R = list(scientific_name_phylo = phylo_cor),
  method = "REML",
  control = list(optimizer = "BFGS"),
  verbose = F
)
saveRDS(
  object = model_SMD_tl,
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/07a_timelag_metamodel_hibernation_OS.RDS'

)

The results above suggest some degree of time-lag bias.

results <- mod_results(model_SMD_tl, mod = "year_scl", group = "Study_ID")
time_bias <- orchaRd::bubble_plot(
  model_SMD_tl,
  mod = 'year_scl',
  group = 'Study_ID',
  alpha = 0.2,
  cb = FALSE,
  xlab = "Year of publication (scaled)",
  transfm = "none",
) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, angle = 0),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16)
  )

ggsave(

Endotherms vs. ectotherms:

Now, we investigate if the response to hibernation varies across biomarkers of oxidative stress for endotherms and ectotherms. We include four markers:

table(df_SMD$Biomarker_cat_2)
## 
##      Antioxidant Oxidative_damage       Regulatory              ROS 
##              582              102               34               24

Meta-model for endotherms:

## data for SMD
df_SMD_endo <- df_SMD %>%
  filter(!is.na(SMDH)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(SMDH.sv)) %>%
  filter(Thermoregulation == 'Endothermic')

## calculate var-cover matrix to control for correlated effect sizes within study and tissue
V_endo <- vcalc(
  vi = SMDH.sv,
  cluster = Study_ID,
  subgroup = Tissue,
  grp1 = Hib_M,
  grp2 = Euthermia_M,
  w1 = Hib_N,
  w2 = Euthermia_N,
  data = df_SMD_endo
)
  • Number of observation with non-missing SMD: 443
  • Number of studies in the dataset for analysis: 36
  • Number of species in the dataset for analysis: 13
model_SMD_endo <- rma.mv(
  yi = SMDH,
  V = V_endo,
  mods = ~ Biomarker_cat_2 - 1,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | scientific_name_phylo,
    ~ 1 | Species,
    ~ 1 | obsID,
    ~ 1 | Study_ID
  ),
  data = df_SMD_endo,
  R = list(scientific_name_phylo = phylo_cor),
  method = "REML",
  control = list(optimizer = "BFGS"),
  verbose = F
)
saveRDS(
  object = model_SMD_endo,
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/04a_metareg_hibernation_endo_OS.RDS'
  )
)
model_SMD_endo <- readRDS(
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/04a_metareg_hibernation_endo_OS.RDS'
  )
)
summary(model_SMD_endo)

## sigma^2.3  0.7414  0.8610    436     no                  obsID   no

Meta-model for ectotherms:

## data for SMD
df_SMD_ecto <- df_SMD %>%
  filter(!is.na(SMDH)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(SMDH.sv)) %>%
  filter(Thermoregulation == 'Ectothermic')

## calculate var-cover matrix to control for correlated effect sizes within study and tissue
V_ecto <- vcalc(
  vi = SMDH.sv,
  cluster = Study_ID,
  subgroup = Tissue,
  grp1 = Hib_M,
  grp2 = Euthermia_M,
  w1 = Hib_N,
  w2 = Euthermia_N,
  data = df_SMD_ecto
)
  • Number of observation with non-missing SMD: 299
  • Number of studies in the dataset for analysis: 18
  • Number of species in the dataset for analysis: 13
model_SMD_ecto <- rma.mv(
  yi = SMDH,
  V = V_ecto,
  mods = ~ Biomarker_cat_2 - 1,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | Study_ID,
    ~ 1 | scientific_name_phylo,
    ~ 1 | Species,
    ~ 1 | obsID
  ),
  data = df_SMD_ecto,
  R = list(scientific_name_phylo = phylo_cor),
  method = "REML"
)
saveRDS(
  object = model_SMD_ecto,
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/05a_metareg_ecto_hibernation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
model_SMD_ecto <- readRDS(
  file = here(
    './04_models/01_hibernation/05a_metareg_ecto_hibernation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
summary(model_SMD_ecto)
